# CR-009 — Automation recipes + quote triggers / สูตรอัตโนมัติและทริกเกอร์ใบเสนอราคา

**Status:** approved (Boss, 2026-08-09) · **Mode:** DDD
**Plan ref:** `implementation-plan-2026-08-09.md` §5 (ZUMP01 Phase 4) · **Design ref:** `smart-crm-design-2026-08-08.md` §5

## Problem / ปัญหา

CR-007 makes quote outcomes real, but nothing *acts* on them: a quote that has sat unanswered for a
week produces no follow-up, and one that ages out at 90 days closes silently with nobody told. The
automation engine has seven triggers, none of which knows quotes exist.
CR-007 บันทึกผลใบเสนอราคาได้แล้ว แต่ไม่มีอะไรทำงานต่อ — เงียบ 7 วันก็ไม่มีใครตาม, ครบ 90 วันก็ปิดเงียบๆ

Two hazards found during recon shape this CR as much as the feature does:

1. **Message interpolation supports exactly one variable.** `actionExecutor.js` replaces `{{name}}`
   and nothing else, so any other placeholder in a template — `{{quoteNo}}`, `{{daysSince}}` — is
   **sent to the customer as literal braces**. Recipes that need more than a name cannot be written
   safely today.
2. **There is no dry-run.** The design requires recipes to be provable before they can message real
   customers, and no such path exists.

## Decisions / การตัดสินใจ

**1. Two quote triggers, no new worker.** `EVENT_QUOTE_STALE` (sent, still `open`, N days old) and
`EVENT_QUOTE_AGED` (the moment CR-007's worker marks it `lost_no_response`). Both are dispatched
from the **existing** `workers/quote-aging` worker, which already scans exactly this table on
exactly this cadence. Adding a second worker to ask the same question would be duplication.

**2. An interpolation allowlist — and `price`/`amount` are not on it.** `src/lib/automationTemplating.js`
defines the complete set of variables a template may use: `name`, `quoteNo`, `daysSinceSent`,
`companyName`. **No money field is interpolable, by construction.** The design's rule "no action
sends a price that a human has not approved" is enforced here structurally rather than by
reviewer vigilance: a template *cannot* reference an amount because the renderer has no such
variable. Unknown placeholders are rejected at save time (`400`) and stripped at render time — a
customer never receives raw `{{…}}`.

**3. Recipes do not read imported segment candidates.** The design says an insight may drive
automation only after a named human promotes it, and the promotion UI does not exist yet
(CR-008 lands candidates as candidates). Rather than fake it, the dormant recipe is built on
`TIME_INACTIVE`, which Zuri computes from its own data. Referencing imported segments waits for
the promotion surface — stated in Out of scope, not quietly assumed.

## Change / การแก้

| # | Piece | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Trigger vocabulary** | Add `EVENT_QUOTE_STALE` and `EVENT_QUOTE_AGED` to `VALID_TRIGGER_TYPES` (`src/app/api/automations/route.js:10`) and to the `triggerType` comment in `prisma/schema.prisma` (comment only — the column is a free `String`, so **no migration**). |
| 2 | **Dispatch from the quote worker** | `src/app/api/workers/quote-aging/route.js`: (a) when a quote is aged to `lost_no_response`, dispatch `EVENT_QUOTE_AGED` (skipped when no tenant workflow subscribes — m10); (b) add a second scan for quotes `status='SENT'`, `outcome='open'`, `staleNotifiedAt IS NULL`, `issuedAt <=` N days ago (N from the firing workflow's own `triggerConfig.staleDays`, default 7, no upper bound), dispatch `EVENT_QUOTE_STALE`, then stamp `Quote.staleNotifiedAt` (Opus review gate M1 — a rolling date window was tried first and rejected: it is only idempotent if the worker runs on an exact 24h cadence forever, and a late run silently drops the quote rather than notifying it late). Dispatch goes through the engine's existing `dispatchEventWorkflow`, so cooldown and CR-003 consent apply unchanged — the circuit breaker/hourly-rate-limit/`maxExecutionsPerDay` do NOT apply to either event, exactly as they have never applied to any `EVENT_*` trigger (see AC5). Because dispatch is triggerType-scoped rather than workflow-scoped, `runWorkflowForCustomer` additionally gates each `EVENT_QUOTE_STALE` workflow on its own `triggerConfig.staleDays` against the event's real `daysSinceSent` (Opus review gate M2), so two workflows at different thresholds don't both fire off one dispatch. The `triggerEvent` payload carries `{ quoteId, quoteNo, daysSinceSent }`, `daysSinceSent` always computed from the quote's real `issuedAt` (m3) — **ids and counts, never the amount**. A dispatch failure must not abort the aging pass (per-item catch, logged). |
| 3 | **Safe templating** — `src/lib/automationTemplating.js` (new) | `TEMPLATE_VARS = ['name','quoteNo','daysSinceSent','companyName']`. `renderTemplate(text, ctx)` substitutes only those and strips any other `{{…}}`. `validateTemplate(text)` returns the offending placeholders so the workflow API can reject at save time. `actionExecutor`'s `SEND_LINE_MESSAGE`/`SEND_FB_MESSAGE` use `renderTemplate` instead of the current single `.replace(/\{\{name\}\}/g, …)` — same behaviour for `{{name}}`, no literal braces ever again. |
| 4 | **Save-time validation** | `POST/PATCH /api/automations` rejects `400` when any action message contains a placeholder outside the allowlist, naming it. This is where "no unapproved price" becomes enforceable: `{{amount}}` is simply not a variable that exists. |
| 5 | **Dry-run** — `POST /api/automations/[id]/dry-run` (new) | Body `{ customerId }`. Evaluates the workflow's conditions against that customer and returns **what would happen** — `{ matched, conditionResults, actions: [{ type, preview }] }` — where `preview` is the *rendered* message text. **Executes nothing**: no message, no tag, no task, no stage change, no webhook, no execution row, no cooldown consumed. `{ domain:'marketing', action:'R' }` (a read of intent, not a write). Implemented by a `dryRun` flag threaded into the executor that returns each action's would-be effect and returns before any side effect. |
| 6 | **Recipes** — extend `TEMPLATES` in `src/app/api/automations/templates/route.js` | `TPL_QUOTE_FOLLOWUP_7D` — `EVENT_QUOTE_STALE` (`staleDays: 7`) → `NOTIFY_STAFF` + `CREATE_TASK` ("ตามใบเสนอราคา {{quoteNo}}") + `SEND_LINE_MESSAGE` (polite check-in, **no price**, consent-gated by CR-003 automatically). `TPL_QUOTE_AGED_LOST` — `EVENT_QUOTE_AGED` → `CREATE_TASK` + `LOG_ACTIVITY` only; deliberately **no customer message**, because a customer who has been silent for 90 days should not receive an automated nudge announcing we gave up. `TPL_DORMANT_REACTIVATION` — `TIME_INACTIVE` (180 days) + condition `lifecycleStage IN [won/paid roles]` → `NOTIFY_STAFF` + `CREATE_TASK`. `TPL_OCCASION_NEWYEAR` — `TIME_SCHEDULED` (cron in early December, `Asia/Bangkok`) → `NOTIFY_STAFF` + `CREATE_TASK` for the sales team to plan the New Year push. All Thai-first copy. All four ship **inactive**; a human turns them on. |
| 7 | **Flex templates** — `src/lib/line/flexTemplates.js` (already existed for `buildReceiptFlex`; these two builders are appended, not a new file) | Minimal, named builders returning LINE Flex JSON: `quoteFollowUpFlex({ quoteNo, daysSinceSent })` and a `simpleNoticeFlex({ title, body })`. **No builder accepts a price/amount parameter** — decision 2 applies to Flex as much as to text. Ship ready and tested but **unwired**: no tenant-level "Flex enabled" field exists in the schema, so `actionExecutor.js` sends plain text unconditionally until one is added (Opus review gate M6, accepted deviation — see Out of scope). |
| 8 | **Tests** | Templating: allowlisted vars render; `{{amount}}`/`{{price}}`/unknown are stripped at render **and** rejected at save; `{{name}}` behaviour is byte-identical to today (regression). Dispatch: a 91-day quote produces exactly one `EVENT_QUOTE_AGED`; a stale quote produces exactly one `EVENT_QUOTE_STALE` and `staleNotifiedAt` prevents it firing again on a later run (M1); a dispatch throw does not abort the aging pass; the payload key set contains no amount; two `EVENT_QUOTE_STALE` workflows at different `staleDays` only fire the one whose threshold the quote has reached (M2, `runWorkflowForCustomer`); `EVENT_QUOTE_AGED` is not dispatched when no tenant workflow subscribes (m10). Dry-run: returns previews and — asserted explicitly — calls **no** send/tag/task/stage/webhook function and creates no execution row; an action with no `config` returns a `{ success: false }` result rather than 500ing the route (m4). Recipes: every shipped template passes `validateTemplate`, ships `isActive:false`, and `TPL_QUOTE_AGED_LOST` contains no customer-message action. |

## Acceptance Criteria / เกณฑ์ยอมรับ

- **AC1** No system-held money value can be interpolated into a customer message: no money
  variable exists in the templating allowlist, no builder reachable from an automation recipe
  takes a price (`buildReceiptFlex` in `flexTemplates.js` is a pre-existing receipt-dispatch
  template, not reachable from any automation action, and is out of scope here — see m7/m8 below),
  and a template containing `{{amount}}`/`{{price}}` is rejected at save time. (Asserted three
  ways.) This guarantee is about interpolation only — nothing stops a human recipe author from
  typing a literal number into a message's free text; that is an authoring-review problem, not one
  this CR closes.
- **AC2** A customer never receives a literal `{{…}}` placeholder — unknown placeholders are
  stripped at render, and `{{name}}` renders exactly as it does today.
- **AC3** A quote aged by CR-007's worker dispatches exactly one `EVENT_QUOTE_AGED`; a quote that
  reaches a workflow's configured `staleDays` (default 7) and is still open dispatches exactly one
  `EVENT_QUOTE_STALE` for that workflow, and is never re-dispatched for it again (enforced by a
  `Quote.staleNotifiedAt` marker — Opus review gate M1 — not a date window, because a window cannot
  catch up after a missed/late worker run). A tenant running two `EVENT_QUOTE_STALE` workflows at
  different `staleDays` thresholds only fires the one whose threshold the quote has actually
  reached (Opus review gate M2).
- **AC4** Dry-run performs zero side effects — no message, tag, task, stage change, webhook,
  execution row, or cooldown consumption — and returns the rendered previews.
- **AC5** Cooldown and CR-003's consent gate apply to the new triggers, unchanged (regression
  tests). The circuit breaker, the hourly rate limit (`HOURLY_RATE_LIMIT`), and execution counters
  live in `processWorkflowBatch`, which only the cron scan (`handleCronScan`) calls — they have
  never applied to any `EVENT_*` trigger, including the two added here, and still do not.
  `maxExecutionsPerDay` (an `AutomationWorkflow` column) is enforced NOWHERE in the codebase, for
  any trigger type; that is recorded here as a pre-existing gap this CR did not introduce and does
  not close, not assumed away. (Opus review gate B1/B2 — an earlier draft of this AC asserted all
  four protections applied uniformly; that was wrong, not merely imprecise.)
- **AC6** All four recipes ship inactive and pass template validation.
- **AC7** `npm run lint` + targeted vitest + `npm run test:scripts` green; `npx prisma validate` passes.

## Out of scope / นอกขอบเขต

- **Recipes driven by imported segment candidates** — needs the human promotion surface first
  (design §5: automation may reference an insight only after a named human promotes it). The
  dormant recipe therefore uses `TIME_INACTIVE`, not CR-008's `segment_candidates`.
- A visual recipe builder, per-recipe analytics, and A/B variants.
- **Adding `maxExecutionsPerDay`/circuit-breaker/rate-limit coverage to `EVENT_*` triggers** — per
  AC5, none of that has ever applied to event triggers, before or after this CR; making it apply is
  a real change to `automationEngine.js`'s dispatch semantics, not something this CR's scope covers
  (Opus review gate B1/B2 — the original wording, "this CR only proves they still apply," implied a
  guarantee that was never true and so cannot be "proven").
- **Wiring the Flex builders into `actionExecutor.js`'s send path** — `quoteFollowUpFlex`/
  `simpleNoticeFlex` (`src/lib/line/flexTemplates.js`) ship ready and tested, but no tenant-level
  "Flex enabled" config field exists in the schema; inventing one was judged out of this CR's scope
  (Opus review gate M6, accepted deviation). `SEND_LINE_MESSAGE` sends plain text unconditionally
  until that field exists and a future change wires the choice.
- Sending Flex by default (opt-in per tenant; plain text remains the default path).
- The `WEBHOOK` action's outbound URL (pre-existing; note that it remains an export path a tenant
  admin controls, unchanged here).

## Rollout / การปล่อย

One additive migration: `Quote.staleNotifiedAt` (nullable `DateTime`, Opus review gate M1) — the
once-only marker `listStaleCandidates` filters on instead of a date window. No other schema change;
`triggerType` stays a `String` column plus a comment. Recipes ship inactive, so deploy is otherwise
behaviour-neutral until someone enables one. The new dispatches ride the existing `quote-aging`
worker — which, per CR-007's note, does not run in production until the `ZURI_QSTASH_*` env-name
mismatch is resolved.

`TPL_OCCASION_NEWYEAR` additionally cannot fire until `TIME_SCHEDULED` itself is fixed (Opus review
gate B3): `workers/automation-engine/route.js` imports `HOURLY_RATE_LIMIT`, `findScheduledCandidates`,
and `isScheduledWorkflowDue` from `automationEngine.js`, and none of the three exist there — every
`TIME_SCHEDULED` workflow throws inside `handleCronScan` and is swallowed every hour on `main`
today. That fix is out of this CR (tracked separately); the recipe ships inactive with its
`description` noting the dependency rather than silently shipping something that can never run.
